resolved_by: Wooden v. United States, 142 S. Ct. 1063 (2022), which abrogated United States v. Abbott, 794 F.3d 896 (8th Cir. 2015), and adopted the multi-factored 'occasions' inquiry.
issue: Under the ACCA occasions clause, may predicate offenses be treated as committed on different occasions merely because they were committed at different moments in time, or must the court apply a holistic, multi-factored inquiry?

sides.position: Offenses are committed on different occasions if some time elapsed between them; a temporal separation alone is sufficient.
cases: United States v. Abbott, 794 F.3d 896 (8th Cir. 2015)
United States v. Stowell, 40 F.4th 882 (8th Cir. 2022)

quote: Wooden resolved a split of authority between circuits—including the Eighth—that found the ACCA occasions clause satisfied “whenever crimes take place at different moments in time,” and those that undertook “a more holistic inquiry.”
cite: United States v. Christopher Stowell, 40 F.4th 882 (8th Cir. 2022)
